# Pilot — US National Weather Service (CAP)

**Real data.** Generated by `tools/adapters/cap.py` from the live NWS alerts API, which
publishes Common Alerting Protocol content as GeoJSON.

```bash
python3 tools/adapters/cap.py --limit 25 --out examples/pilot-nws-alerts
```

25 live alerts from a feed carrying 157.

## The profile held

Real CAP validated **first time, with zero unmapped values**. Every enumeration mapped
directly — status, message type, severity, urgency, certainty, category, response type — and
no schema change was needed to accept the data.

That is the clearest evidence so far for the rule in [SPEC §1.4](../../SPEC.md): model on the
incumbent standard rather than inventing one. `alerts` was built from the CAP specification
without ever seeing a CAP feed, and real CAP fit it.

## One real defect, and it mattered

**The profile required `references` on an update or cancel.** Ten of twenty-five alerts in
this batch were Updates, and every one superseded an alert that had already expired out of the
active feed.

Faced with that, the adapter's only conformant option was to downgrade `messageType` from
`update` to `alert` — which turns *"this supersedes an earlier warning"* into *"this is a new
warning"*. For a warning system that is not a rounding error; it is the wrong message.

The requirement was right in principle and unsatisfiable in practice, because **alert feeds
are windowed**. `referencesIdentifier` now carries the CAP identifier of a superseded alert
that is not in the dataset, and an update or cancel must supply one or the other. Message
types are preserved as published:

```
messageType in output: alert 15, update 10
carrying referencesIdentifier: 10
```

## Still open: geometry

The profile references geometry by URL rather than embedding it, on the grounds that a
warning polygon is thousands of coordinate pairs and alerts travel over constrained channels.
NWS **inlines** the polygon as GeoJSON in the same document.

The adapter currently links to the alert's own API endpoint, which resolves to the whole alert
rather than to a geometry resource. That is a workaround, not a mapping, and it is the
clearest case yet for the unresolved geospatial question in
[ROADMAP.md](../../ROADMAP.md) — a publisher that inlines geometry has nowhere to put it under
the current design.

Of this batch, 15 carried an inline polygon and 10 gave only zone references.

## Other observations

**One sender.** CAP `sender` is an email-style address rather than an identified
organization, so issuing offices carry a `local:` identifier. There is no equivalent of
org-id.guide for emergency-management offices.

**Two alerts carried no `instruction`** — informative rather than actionable. The profile
treats `instruction` as what makes an alert actionable and correctly leaves it optional.

**A bug in the adapter, not the profile:** NWS encodes `category` and `response` as bare
strings when there is one value, so the first run iterated them character by character and
reported `category:M`, `category:e`, `category:t`. CAP allows these to repeat; the JSON
encoding does not always show it.
